sentences.text:
Appearance:
 Shri Gaurav Mishra - advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Rohit Shrivastava P.L. for the respondent/State.
ORDER Heard on I.A.No.9944 of 2025 for taking documents on record.
The documents may be relevant for proper adjudication of the matter, therefore, the IA is allowed and documents are taken on record.
Also heard on I.A.No.9945 of 2025 for exemption from filing affidavit.
Since the applicant is in jail, therefore, this application is allowed and the applicant is exempted from filing affidavit in the matter.

This first bail application has been filed by applicant under Section 483 of the BNSS 2023 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No. 05 of 2025 registered at Police Station Bhaguapura distt. Datia for offences punishable under Sections 305, 376 and 34 of IPC and 3/4 of POCSO Act.
The applicant is in judicial custody since 11/01/2025.

As per the case of prosecution story, the present applicant is father of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:10277 2 MCRC-17975-2025 the co-accused Rohit.

Allegation against him is that he denied marriage of the prosecutrix with his son Rohit and on the pretext of marriage, co-accused Rohit established sexual relationship with the prosecutrix and thereafter, denied marriage,
therefore, the deceased committed suicide.
After merg intimation, offence has been registered against the present applicant.

sentences.text: Learned Counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated.
The applicant is 65 years of age having no criminal past.
Only omnibus allegations have been levied against him.
After incident, parents of the deceased did not state anything against him but after lapse of 11 months, allegations have been levied against the applicant.

Parents of the deceased (PW1) and (Pw2) both have been examined before the trial court but they turned hostile and did not state anything against the present applicant in respect of the aforesaid offence.
The applicant is not main accused.
He is permanent resident of distt. Datia.
Trial would take time to conclude.
Therefore, applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.
Per contra, learned Counsel for the State opposes the bail application and prayed for rejection.
But fairly admits that no criminal antecedents are reported against the applicant.
Both the parties are heard and perused the Case Diary.

Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, arguments advanced by counsel for the parties, and also taking note of the fact that the parents of the deceased have turned hostile, only omnibus allegations have been levied against the p r e s e n t a p p l i c a n t a f t e r l a p s e o f 1 1 m o n t h s o f t h e N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .
2025:MPHC-GWL:10277 3 MCRC-17975-2025 incident and the applicant is not main accused and the trial would take time to conclude
, therefore, I deem it proper to release the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.75,000/- (Rupees Seventy Five Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court, as and when required.
He shall abide by the conditions enumerated u/S. 437(3) Cr.P.C./480(3) of BNSS.
Certified copy as per rules.
